_comment: The ordered sub-goals of COOHAVIOR S1-V4-LL, which the BDDL beside this
file cannot state. Read by coop2.behavior_env.route_spec; the design is
coop2/ROUTE_SUPERVISION_PLAN.md section 5.1.
Transcribed from COOHAVIOR/behavior_style_task/tasks.modified.json, entry
S1-V4-LL, route S1-M5 -- checkpoints C1..C9 in `sequence` order, then the
destination `fixture_bddl_instance` bed.n.01_1 at station M5. That file,
not their BDDL, is what COOHAVIOR runs: their S1-V4-LL.bddl still says a
bedroom floor.
Order is list order. There is no `sequence` and no `depends_on`: the
only order COOHAVIOR enforces is checkpoint sequence, and its five
`packages` are this one box's five legs, read by no runtime code.
Support ids are our numbering of our synsets, declared in problem0.bddl:
C1  cabinet.n.01_1               COOHAVIOR cabinet.n.01_5         bottom_cabinet_dajebq_0  childs_room
C2  bookcase.n.01_1              shelf.n.01_3                     shelf_owvfik_0 = our bookcase_owvfik_0  kitchen
C3  electric_refrigerator.n.01_1 fridge.n.01_1 (not a synset here) fridge_xyejdx_0          kitchen
C4  armchair.n.01_1              armchair.n.01_1                  armchair_qplklw_2        dining_room
C5  breakfast_table.n.01_1       breakfast_table.n.01_2           breakfast_table_rjgmmy_0 dining_room
C6  coffee_table.n.01_1          coffee_table.n.01_1              coffee_table_fqluyq_0    living_room
C7  cabinet.n.01_2               bottom_cabinet.n.01_1 (not a synset here) bottom_cabinet_jhymlr_0  living_room
C8  cabinet.n.01_3               bottom_cabinet.n.01_2 (not a synset here) bottom_cabinet_jrhgeu_0  bedroom
C9  bed.n.01_2                   bed.n.01_2                       bed_zrumze_1             bedroom
D   bed.n.01_1                   bed.n.01_1                       bed_zrumze_0             childs_room
C2: COOHAVIOR calls the support shelf_owvfik_0; our dataset ships the
same model owvfik as bookcase_owvfik_0, category bookcase, at the same
pose (-0.17, 4.90) in kitchen_0. Same object, older asset name -- so the
node says bookcase.n.01_1, which is what the sampler can bind.
What the 2026-09-12 re-sample actually bound (the sampler prints this):
C4 -> armchair_qplklw_1, not COOHAVIOR's _2 (the one V4 moves): inroom
dining_room matches all three qplklw armchairs and the sampler took _1,
which _apply_scene_edits then kept off V4's deactivate list because the
BDDL bound it -- so this scene had one armchair more than V4's, and one
more than LH/HL/HH, whose samples bound _2 and let _1 be deleted.
Corrected by hand on 2026-09-15 (user): _1 removed from the instance and
C4 rebound to armchair_qplklw_2, the row above. Nothing referenced _1 --
one armchair is declared, the goal is ontop(die, bed), and C4 is the only
node that uses a chair -- so the four S1 tasks now share one dining room
and C4 means the same object in all of them. C8 ->
bottom_cabinet_jrhgeu_1, not _0; both stand in bedroom_0 and COOHAVIOR's
own files disagree on which. Neither changes the route; both are
recorded so a run's plan_logs can be read against the right object.
C5's table is model rjgmmy at native scale (0.75 x 0.94 x 0.58 m), not
the scene's own skczfi scaled to 0.92 x 1.52 x 0.79 (user, 2026-09-14:
a smaller table), stood against the dining room's north wall at
(-0.996, 8.213), long side east-west.
lift: the 8 g die may be carried by an arm or the drone. The 20 g
notebook of LH/HH may not be lifted by the drone; that table lives in
those tasks' route files.
